# cloudscape

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/ehsanrahimi666/cloudscape/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ehsanrahimi666/cloudscape/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/ehsanrahimi666/cloudscape/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/)
![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.2.0-35978f)![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-GPL--3-8073ac)

**Clear-observation availability and cloud analysis for optical
satellite image time series.**

Cloud masks tell you which pixels are cloudy. Planning a time-series
study also needs three other answers: how many usable observations
remain at the study site, when in the year they occur, and how the gaps
affect the quantity you want to estimate. `cloudscape` links these steps
in one R workflow:

- it queries SpatioTemporal Asset Catalogs (no account needed) and keeps
  the latest processing version of every acquisition;
- it aggregates acquisitions onto an **equal-area grid** (EASE-Grid
  2.0), so counts refer to the same area for every sensor and latitude;
- it records the **evidence tier** of every count: usability inferred
  from scene-level cloud cover, or measured within each grid cell from
  the producer quality layers (Landsat `QA_PIXEL`, Sentinel-2 `SCL`);
- it summarises usable counts, gaps, seasonality and cloud persistence,
  with every statistic carrying its unit, sample size and denominator;
- it propagates an acquisition record into the **simulated error of
  phenological dates** (start, peak and end of season) under stated
  assumptions.

![The cloudscape workflow](reference/figures/readme-workflow.png)

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ehsanrahimi666/cloudscape")
```

The statistical core depends only on base R. `terra`, `sf` and `httr2`
are suggested and loaded only when raster or network functionality is
used, so the package installs and runs its test suite without a GDAL
toolchain.

## How it works: a worked example at Andong, Republic of Korea

The figures below come from the analysis in
[`analysis/`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/analysis),
which reproduces every number of the accompanying article from archived
inputs (Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9, 2019–2024, sixteen 25 km cells).

### 1. Define an equal-area study area and find what exists

``` r

library(cloudscape)
grid  <- cl_grid(res = 25000)                    # EASE-Grid 2.0, 25 km cells
site  <- cl_grid_cells(grid, cl_grid_lookup(grid, 128.73, 36.57))
cells <- as.vector(outer((site$row + -3:0) * grid$ncol, site$col + -2:1, "+"))
xy    <- cl_grid_cells(grid, cells)
ll    <- cl_unproject(range(xy$x) + c(-1, 1) * grid$res / 2,
                      range(xy$y) + c(-1, 1) * grid$res / 2)
aoi   <- c(ll[1, "lon"], ll[1, "lat"], ll[2, "lon"], ll[2, "lat"])

items <- cl_search(aoi, "sentinel-2-msi", "2019-01-01", "2024-12-31", limit = Inf)
```

Landsat scenes and Sentinel-2 tiles cover the same ground with
footprints of different size and placement; the grid cells do not change
between sensors.

![Study area, cells and
footprints](reference/figures/readme-study_area.png)

### 2. Scene metadata or quality layers?

``` r

meta <- cl_items_to_obs(items, grid)      # scene-level cloud cover, every covered cell
qa   <- cl_qa_obs(items, grid, cells)     # cloud fraction measured within each cell
```

A scene’s cloud cover is an average over its footprint. On the overpass
below (12 June 2024), the four Sentinel-2 tiles report 5–35% cloud and
every cell inherits 34–35% from them, so no cell passes a 20% screen.
The quality layer shows that seven of the sixteen cells were usable and
others were completely overcast.

![One overpass: true colour, scene classification and cell cloud
fractions](reference/figures/readme-scene_example.png)

Across all acquisitions, the two evidence tiers can be compared
directly, with confidence intervals that resample whole overpasses:

![Scene cloud cover against cell cloud
fraction](reference/figures/readme-scene_vs_cell.png)

### 3. How many usable observations, where and when?

``` r

cl_clear_obs(qa, by = "year")       # usable observations per cell and year
cl_gaps(qa, critical = 21)          # longest stretch without a usable observation
cl_seasonality(qa, harmonics = 2)   # seasonal cycle and best acquisition window
cl_persistence(qa)                  # decorrelation time, with and without the seasonal cycle
```

![Acquisition record of one cell](reference/figures/readme-timeline.png)

![Usable observations and gaps per
cell](reference/figures/readme-cell_maps.png)

![Seasonal usability by evidence
tier](reference/figures/readme-seasonality.png)

### 4. What does the record mean for phenology?

``` r

pheno <- cl_pheno_map(qa, year = 2024, n_sim = 200, threshold = 0.2,
                      noise = 0.03, persistence = 0.35, seed = 20241)
```

Each cell’s actual acquisition dates and cloud fractions are used to
sample a known double-logistic trajectory, which is refitted 200 times.
The result is a simulated error, in days, of the start, peak and end of
season, and the share of failed retrievals. These values depend on the
assumed curve, noise and cloud persistence; they describe the
information in the acquisition record, not the accuracy of a retrieval
from real data.

![Simulated phenological errors](reference/figures/readme-phenology.png)

## Quick start without a network connection

``` r

library(cloudscape)
d <- seq(as.Date("2024-01-01"), as.Date("2024-12-31"), by = "5 days")
for (cf in c(0.3, 0.6, 0.85)) {
  r <- cl_pheno_power(d, cloud_fraction = cf, n_sim = 200, seed = 1)
  print(round(r$summary[, c("n_usable_median", "sos_mae", "peak_mae",
                            "eos_mae", "failure_rate")], 2))
}
#>   n_usable_median sos_mae peak_mae eos_mae failure_rate
#> 1            52.5     0.9      3.6     0.9            0
#>   n_usable_median sos_mae peak_mae eos_mae failure_rate
#> 1              30     1.4      6.2     1.4         0.03
#>   n_usable_median sos_mae peak_mae eos_mae failure_rate
#> 1              12     3.1    12.45     4.6         0.39
```

Statistics carry their units and are checked on construction:

``` r

cl_stats(1:2, "cloud_fraction", c(0.3, 1.4))
#> Error: Metric 'cloud_fraction' has value 1.4 outside its permitted range [0, 1] (row 2).
```

## Sensors and detection methods

Drivers are supplied for Landsat 4–9, Sentinel-2, MODIS and a generic
multispectral camera (PlanetScope, WorldView, SPOT, RapidEye, UAV).
Adding a sensor means writing one driver:

``` r

cl_sensor_register(cl_sensor_driver(
  id = "my-sensor", name = "My camera",
  bands = c(blue = "B1", green = "B2", red = "B3", nir = "B4"),
  revisit = 5))
cl_methods(sensor = "my-sensor")   # which algorithms are applicable
```

| Method | Type | Status in 0.2.0 |
|----|----|----|
| `qa` | Producer mask | Implemented: decodes CFMask `QA_PIXEL` and Sen2Cor `SCL` |
| `threshold` | Physical | Implemented: brightness and whiteness baseline |
| `fmask` | Physical | Implemented: decision cascade following Zhu and Woodcock (2012) |
| `s2cloudless`, `randomforest`, `xgboost`, `unet` | Learned | Registered, not implemented; no model weights are distributed |

The pixel-level detectors, the shadow search and the scene simulator are
verified against analytical identities and synthetic scenes, but they
have not been validated against labelled imagery; treat them as
experimental. A trained model can be supplied through
[`cl_method_register()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_method_register.md).

## Reproducing the article’s analysis

From the repository root, run the scripts in `analysis/` in numerical
order (`01_query.R` to `07_numbers.R`). `analysis/config.R` holds every
setting. The catalogue records, quality-layer extracts and image subsets
used in the article are archived in `analysis/data/`, so the scripts
from `03` onwards run without a network connection, except
`05b_scene_example.R`, which downloads the two image subsets again.

## Citation

Rahimi, E. and Jung, C. cloudscape: clear-observation availability and
cloud analysis for optical satellite image time series. R package
version 0.2.0. <https://github.com/ehsanrahimi666/cloudscape>

  : Require a suggested package
- [`cl_manifest()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_manifest.md)
  : Create or extract a provenance manifest

  [`cl_sensor()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/sensor-registry.md)

  : Construct a sensor driver
- [`cl_qa_spec()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_qa_spec.md)
  : Describe a quality-assessment band

## Analysis grid

- [`cl_grid()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_grid.md)
  : Define an equal-area analysis grid

  : Cell identifiers, centroids and areas
- [`cl_grid_index()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_grid_index.md)
  : Index sensor footprints onto the analysis grid

  [`cl_unproject()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_project.md)
  : Project longitude/latitude to and from EASE-Grid 2.0 metres

## Catalogue access

- [`cl_catalog()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_catalog.md)
  : Configure or inspect a catalogue backend

  : Search a catalogue for scenes
- [`cl_items_to_obs()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_items_to_obs.md)
  : Convert catalogue items to an observation table

  : Construct a cloud/shadow mask set

  : Construct a grid statistics table
- [`cl_stats_merge()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_stats_merge.md)
  : Combine statistics tables
- [`cl_stats_wide()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_stats_wide.md)

  : Standard class coding
- [`cl_metrics()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_metrics.md)

  : Validate a statistics table

- [`cl_band()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_band.md)

## Preprocessing

- [`cl_scale()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_scale.md)
  : Rescale stored integers to reflectance
- [`cl_geometry()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_geometry.md)
  : Attach or compute scene geometry
- [`cl_solar_position()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_solar_position.md)
  : Solar position for a location and time
- [`cl_indices()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_indices.md)
  : Common spectral indices

## Cloud detection

- [`cl_probability()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_probability.md)
  : Compute cloud probability
- [`cl_methods()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_methods.md)
  : List available cloud-probability methods
- [`cl_method_register()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_method_register.md)
  : Register a cloud-probability method
- [`cl_qa_decode()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_qa_decode.md)
  : Decode a producer quality layer

## Shadow

- [`cl_shadow()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_shadow.md)
  : Detect cloud shadows
- [`cl_shadow_offset()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_shadow_offset.md)
  : Ground displacement of a cloud shadow
- [`cl_shadow_project()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_shadow_project.md)
  : Project a cloud mask to candidate shadow locations
- [`cl_cloud_height()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_cloud_height.md)
  : Estimate cloud-top height from thermal brightness temperature
- [`cl_terrain_shadow()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_terrain_shadow.md)
  : Cast shadow from terrain

## Uncertainty

- [`cl_agreement()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_agreement.md)
  : Agreement among several masks
- [`cl_disagreement()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_disagreement.md)
  : Pairwise disagreement between masks
- [`cl_reliability()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_reliability.md)
  : Flag conditions where cloud masks are known to be unreliable

## Availability and feasibility

- [`cl_obs()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_obs.md)
  : Build an observation table
- [`cl_clear_obs()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_clear_obs.md)
  : Clear observation counts per cell and period
- [`cl_clear_prob()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_clear_prob.md)
  : Probability that a pixel in a cell is clear
- [`cl_gaps()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_gaps.md)
  : Cloud-gap statistics
- [`cl_seasonality()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_seasonality.md)
  : Seasonal clear-sky model
- [`cl_synergy()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_synergy.md)
  : Multi-constellation revisit synergy
- [`cl_feasibility()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_feasibility.md)
  : Sampling design feasibility
- [`cl_persistence()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_persistence.md)
  : Estimate the temporal persistence of cloud from an observation
  record
- [`cl_qa_obs()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_qa_obs.md)
  : Build a quality-layer observation table

## Phenology

- [`cl_pheno_curve()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_pheno_curve.md)
  : Double-logistic seasonal trajectory
- [`cl_pheno_fit()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_pheno_fit.md)
  : Fit a seasonal trajectory and extract phenological metrics
- [`cl_pheno_power()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_pheno_power.md)
  : Phenological retrieval error under realistic cloud loss
- [`cl_pheno_map()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_pheno_map.md)
  : Map phenological retrieval error across grid cells

## Simulation and evaluation

- [`cl_simulate()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_simulate.md)
  : Simulate clouds and cloud shadows
- [`cl_simulate_series()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_simulate_series.md)
  : Simulate a contaminated time series
- [`cl_validate()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_validate.md)
  : Accuracy metrics for a binary or multi-class mask
- [`cl_confusion()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_confusion.md)
  : Confusion matrix
- [`cl_roc()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_roc.md)
  : ROC curve and area under it
- [`cl_calibration()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_calibration.md)
  : Probability calibration
- [`cl_compare()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_compare.md)
  : Compare methods with uncertainty
- [`cl_benchmark()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_benchmark.md)
  : Load a benchmark dataset

## Performance, visualisation, export

- [`cl_chunk()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_chunk.md)
  : Plan chunked processing of a large raster
- [`cl_apply_chunks()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_apply_chunks.md)
  : Apply a function over chunks, optionally in parallel
- [`cl_visualize()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_visualize.md)
  : Quick look at a mask or scene
- [`cl_explore()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_explore.md)
  : Export an interactive map of grid statistics
- [`cl_app()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_app.md)
  : Launch the interactive scene explorer
- [`cl_export()`](https://ehsanrahimi666.github.io/cloudscape/reference/cl_export.md)
  : Export cloudscape objects
